assertions.description: Element.prototype.requestFullscreen is a function: this is the Fullscreen API whose use Chromium's client-side detection records as the FULLSCREEN_API scam-check trigger.
Without transient activation, requestFullscreen() rejects with a TypeError instead of taking over the screen. A legitimate site can only go fullscreen from a real user gesture.
assertions.test: (async () => { if (navigator.userActivation && navigator.userActivation.isActive) return false; try { await document.documentElement.requestFullscreen(); await document.exitFullscreen(); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: Keyboard.prototype.lock is a function: this is the Keyboard Lock API whose use Chromium records as the KEYBOARD_LOCK_REQUESTED scam-check trigger.
navigator.keyboard.lock() rejects with InvalidAccessError when none of the requested key codes is valid.
Element.prototype.requestPointerLock is a function: this is the Pointer Lock API whose use Chromium records as the POINTER_LOCK_REQUESTED scam-check trigger.
The server-side Gemini scam check runs only for profiles in Enhanced Safe Browsing (SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel = 2). Standard and No Protection profiles are never scanned.
assertions.test: Browser-internal and not observable from a web page: no API exposes the Safe Browsing level or scan activity. Check chrome://settings/security (or chrome://policy for SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel) by hand; see /v155/server-side-gemini-powered-scam-checks-for-desktop/check-your-browser/.

assertions.description: Page text leaves the device only after a high-confidence scam indicator fires, and the server processes it ephemerally (not logged, retained or used for training).
assertions.test: A data-handling commitment that runs inside Chrome and Google's servers, so a page cannot observe it. Source: the ChromeStatus summary. The modelled flow is at /v155/server-side-gemini-powered-scam-checks-for-desktop/data-flow-explorer/.

assertions.description: On desktop, Chrome 155 uses the server-side model (IntelligentScanModelType SERVER_SIDE_MODEL) in place of the earlier on-device Gemini Nano check (ON_DEVICE_MODEL), up to a daily scan quota.
assertions.test: Controlled by the Finch feature kClientSideDetectionServerModelForScamDetectionDesktop (param MaxIntelligentScansPerDayDesktop, source default 5). Only Chrome-internal logging shows which model ran.
